name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,805

entries.clue: Top Charlotte perhaps that 7A 17 wouldn't buy? (6,5)

blocks.note: a jersey is a top, a sweater

annotation.surface: A shopper eyes a pricey top as Princess Charlotte might wear, knowing a skinflint would never pay for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 7A and 17 put together read POT ATOMISER, split as 'potato miser': Jersey Royals are the expensive new potato such a person would pass by. Charlotte is itself a potato variety, a nod to the theme.
annotation.definitionFit: Jersey Royals are costly new potatoes from Jersey, just what a potato miser would refuse to buy.

entries.clue: Various purchases stain after juice tipped (3,3)

indicatorNotes.after: in a down clue, coming after means sitting below, so the stain goes under the juice
indicatorNotes.tipped: a glass tipped over is upended, so OJ is turned upside down in this down entry

annotation.surface: Someone knocks over a glass of juice and ends up with a stain.
annotation.walkthrough: The juice is the standard shorthand for orange juice, and the spill in the surface is exactly what turns it over.
annotation.definitionFit: A job lot is a mixed batch of goods bought together, so a set of various purchases.

entries.clue: Elastic gets old for uniform, a worry for security guard? (7)

indicatorNotes.gets: the elastic word receives something new, the incoming letter
indicatorNotes.for: one thing in exchange for another, so O takes the place of U

blocks.note: O (old) replaces U (uniform, the NATO alphabet word for U)

annotation.surface: A security guard frets that the elastic in his uniform is getting old.
annotation.walkthrough: The uniform looks like the guard's clothing; it is the letter U in the phonetic alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A theft by force is the very thing a security guard is there to prevent, so a worry for one.

entries.clue: Stain entered beneath the first of eight o's (5)

indicatorNotes.beneath: in a down clue, beneath means lower in the column, so the last piece sits under the others
indicatorNotes.the first of: take only the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the plural of the letter O

annotation.surface: Someone notes where a stain landed on a row of eight circles.
annotation.walkthrough: The o's are simply letters written as a plural, not zeros or rings.
annotation.definitionFit: Eosin is a red dye used to stain tissue samples for microscopy.

entries.clue: Tiller that goes up and down? (9)

indicatorNotes.that goes up and down: in a down entry, a word that reads the same going up the column as going down is a palindrome

blocks.note: a word that reads the same upwards and downwards in the grid

annotation.surface: A question about a farm machine that bobs up and down as it works the soil.
annotation.walkthrough: The machine does go up and down over the furrows, but the clue means the word itself, spelt identically either way.
annotation.definitionFit: A Rotavator is a motorised tiller that breaks up soil with rotating blades.

entries.clue: Bound to serve half of your King Edward (5)

indicatorNotes.half of: take half the letters of the next word, here its first two

blocks.note: the first two letters of YOUR

annotation.surface: A subject pledges loyal service to King Edward.
annotation.walkthrough: King Edward reads as a monarch but splits into two pieces; it is also a potato variety, part of the puzzle's theme.
annotation.definitionFit: Oxen yoked together are harnessed to the work of pulling, bound to serve.

entries.clue: Unsociable types bored by fellow citizens (9)

indicatorNotes.bored by: bored as in drilled through, so the second word goes into the first

blocks.note: a don is a college fellow

annotation.surface: Loners find their fellow citizens tedious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bored' looks like tedium but means drilled into. Fellow means a university fellow, not a man.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the people of London are one city's citizens.

entries.clue: Cup to clear from the table (3)

blocks.note: in snooker, sinking a ball takes it off the table

annotation.surface: Someone clears the teacups away after a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: The table is a snooker table, not a dining one.
annotation.definitionFit: Sports slang calls a trophy a pot, and in snooker to pot a ball is to clear it from the table.

entries.clue: Freight left on time (7)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

blocks.note: an age is a period of time

annotation.surface: A cargo ship's freight departed on schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed, but it is the ship's left side, which suits the cargo surface nicely.
annotation.definitionFit: Portage is the carrying of goods, or the charge for it, so freight in both senses.

entries.clue: Irresistible mashed, fried too (2,3,3)

indicatorNotes.mashed: mashed things are crushed out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

annotation.surface: A potato that is mashed and fried as well sounds irresistible.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mashed' fits the potato theme and is the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: something to die for is so desirable it is irresistible.

entries.clue: Chum, say, keeps near sons to watch them (4-3)

indicatorNotes.keeps: to keep something is to hold it, so the first word holds the next pieces inside

blocks.note: chum is fish scraps thrown in as bait
s = son; one S serves for the plural

annotation.surface: A friend stays close to the boys to keep an eye on them.
annotation.walkthrough: Chum looks like a friend, but 'say' flags an example: chum is anglers' bait, chopped fish thrown into the water.
annotation.definitionFit: To babysit is to mind someone's children, and 'them' stands for the sons of the surface.

entries.clue: Stock nice and hot, apparently (7)

blocks.note: red is the colour of heat, as in red-hot

annotation.surface: A soup stock that seems both pleasant and piping hot.
annotation.walkthrough: Stock reads as soup base but means family line.
annotation.definitionFit: Kindred is one's family, the stock one comes from.

entries.clue: Water now overheating changed at once, saving time (5)

indicatorNotes.changed: letters that are changed are rearranged
indicatorNotes.saving: saving in the sense of 'except', so the named letter is left out

blocks.note: AT ONCE with T (time) taken out

annotation.surface: An alarm that the water is overheating and must be changed immediately.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saving' means except, not keeping. The definition points at warming seas.
annotation.definitionFit: The oceans are the body of water now heating up with the climate.

entries.clue: Six ancient characters in salmon river, fun they're too old for? (5,4)

indicatorNotes.in: the ancient characters are put inside the river

blocks.note: the Dee, a Scottish salmon river
ogam (ogham) is an ancient Irish alphabet

annotation.surface: Six old people at a salmon river are thought too old for a bit of fun.
annotation.walkthrough: Characters reads as people but means letters of an old script. The 'they' of the definition are the ancient characters, now too old for modern fun.
annotation.definitionFit: Screen games are modern fun that anyone ancient is supposedly too old for.

entries.clue: Charlie avoids metaphysics that's tricky to understand (10)

indicatorNotes.avoids: Charlie avoids the word, so the letter stays out of it
indicatorNotes.tricky: tricky suggests something twisted and awkward, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Charlie = C in the NATO alphabet, removed

annotation.surface: Charlie steers clear of metaphysics because it is hard to follow.
annotation.walkthrough: Charlie looks like a person but is the letter C.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of sharing and grasping another's feelings: 'I understand' as comfort.

entries.clue: Clean up old man with grim haircut (9)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the word is reversed

blocks.note: MOP (clean) read upwards in this down clue

annotation.surface: Someone tidies up an old man who has a grim haircut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clean up' looks like one phrasal verb; it is a verb followed by a direction.
annotation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a hairstyle swept high off the forehead.

entries.clue: Someone who got what was coming to them? (9)

annotation.definition: Someone who got what was coming to them?

blocks.note: got as in received, not suffered
sounds like deserved punishment; literally, what was due to pass to them

annotation.surface: A remark about someone finally getting their comeuppance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Got what was coming to them' sounds like just deserts; read literally, it is someone receiving what a will left them.
annotation.definitionFit: An heir receives the estate that was due to come to them.

entries.clue: Maybe love one's self (3)

annotation.surface: Advice that perhaps you should love yourself.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests self-love, but 'love' is only the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Latin 'I', used for a person's sense of who they are.

entries.clue: Spray from storm in Timor Sea (8)

indicatorNotes.storm in: a storm churns things up, so the letters in the fodder are tossed about

annotation.surface: Sea spray whipped up by a storm over the Timor Sea.
annotation.walkthrough: Spray and storm set a stormy seascape; the storm is the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An atomiser turns liquid into a fine spray, and the device can be called a spray.

entries.clue: Reduction in blue-green colour makes water browner (3)

indicatorNotes.Reduction in: a reduced word is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: teal is a blue-green shade, cut short by one letter

annotation.surface: Toning down a blue-green shade turns the water a muddier brown.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is loose and playful: the drink is water made browner.
annotation.definitionFit: Tea is water turned brown by the leaves steeped in it.

entries.clue: Label whale starting from the rear flipper? (7)

indicatorNotes.starting from the rear: begin at the back and read forwards, so the letters come in reverse

annotation.surface: Tagging a whale by starting at its tail flipper.
annotation.walkthrough: The flipper is not a fin but someone who does flips; the whale surface makes the fin reading almost irresistible.
annotation.definitionFit: A tumbler performs flips, so is humorously a 'flipper'.

entries.clue: Possible mistake will happen, adding 24 to 1A? (7,3)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition paraphrases the law's content rather than naming it

indicatorNotes.adding: adding one thing to another puts them together, the second after the first

blocks.note: 1A is a potato, and a murphy is slang for a potato
24 is a salad, and slaw is one

annotation.surface: A warning that throwing a salad in with the potatoes is bound to go wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: Both pieces go through other answers: the potato at 1A becomes Irish slang for a potato, and the salad at 24 becomes a specific salad.
annotation.definitionFit: Murphy's law says anything that can go wrong will go wrong.

entries.clue: Fatty ordered pie and soda (7)

indicatorNotes.ordered: letters put in order are arranged afresh

annotation.surface: A fat person orders pie and a fizzy drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Fatty reads as a person placing an order, and it is the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical synonym, used of body tissue that stores fat.

entries.clue: River choked by sediment not so nice now (6)

indicatorNotes.choked by: the river is choked by the sediment, so the sediment closes around it

annotation.surface: A river clogged with sediment is less pleasant than it was.
annotation.walkthrough: The Po is the crossword's favourite river; here it lodges after the first letter of the sediment.
annotation.definitionFit: Something spoilt has been ruined, no longer as nice as it was.

entries.clue: Germans cooked King Edward, presenting fish-eater with bill (9)

indicatorNotes.cooked: cooked as in cooked up or falsified, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Edwardus Rex, the royal cipher, part of the fodder

annotation.surface: German cooks serve King Edward potatoes to a diner along with the bill.
annotation.walkthrough: King Edward is a potato variety, apt for 'cooked'; here it is the royal cipher, which joins the mix. The bill is a beak.
annotation.definitionFit: The merganser is a fish-eating duck with a slender serrated bill.

entries.clue: Upset daughter regrettably shows cold side (5)

indicatorNotes.Upset: set upside down, which in a down clue reverses the word

annotation.surface: A daughter, upset, sadly gives someone the cold shoulder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' belongs to the word for regrettably, though it sits beside daughter. The side is a side dish.
annotation.definitionFit: Restaurant shorthand: a side is a side dish, and this one is served cold.

entries.clue: Authoritative police officer grabs teacher from behind (5)

indicatorNotes.grabs: to grab is to seize and hold, so the officer holds the teacher
indicatorNotes.from behind: read from the back, so the combination is reversed

blocks.note: sir, what pupils call a male teacher

annotation.surface: A commanding policeman seizes a teacher from behind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From behind' looks like the direction of the arrest but applies to the whole assembly.
annotation.definitionFit: A crisp manner is brisk and decisive, the tone of authority.

entries.clue: US police show cool in case of crisis (5)

indicatorNotes.case of: a word's case is its outside, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A US police drama keeps its cool in a crisis.
annotation.walkthrough: In case of crisis reads as a safety notice; case means the word's shell.
annotation.definitionFit: CHiPs was a US television show about California Highway Patrol officers.

entries.clue: Small Swiss bank given BP's business finds hidden dirt (7)

annotation.surface: A minor Swiss bank takes on BP's account and turns up concealed scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: Hidden dirt reads as buried scandal; it is literal earth under the topsoil.
annotation.definitionFit: Subsoil is the layer of earth lying hidden beneath the topsoil.

entries.clue: City I see returning after holiday (7)

indicatorNotes.returning: coming back, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.after: the reversed piece comes after the holiday

blocks.note: I + LO (see, as in lo and behold), turned around

annotation.surface: A traveller spots a city on the way home from holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' is the old exclamation lo, as in 'lo and behold', not the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the capital of Libya is one city.

entries.clue: Verity's inside a trench (3)

indicatorNotes.inside: the inside of a word is everything but its first and last letters

blocks.note: verity = TRUTH; take its middle, dropping the outer T and H

annotation.surface: Someone called Verity is sitting in a trench.
annotation.walkthrough: Verity looks like a woman's name but is the word for truth.
annotation.definitionFit: A rut is a long groove worn in the ground, a small trench.

entries.clue: Washington research probes lately formed humanitarian group (3,8)

indicatorNotes.probes: a probe pokes inside something, so the first pieces go into the last

annotation.surface: A Washington study looks into a newly founded aid organisation.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one think-tank investigating another; 'probes' is literal, pushing letters inside.
annotation.definitionFit: The Red Crescent is the Red Cross movement's counterpart in Muslim countries.
